7. Rehabilitation and Code Enforcement
When completed, a large number of the properties within the project will have been rehabilitated to the applicable standards established for the project area under the urban renewal plan. This set of standards will closely resemble Harrisburg's city code requirements. Where needed, the City's authority to enforce its building and housing codes will be brought into play to provide the necessary conformance to city housing code requirements. By the time of project completion it is anticipated, that all of the 565 buildings designated for rehabilitation will have been rehabilitated and that all will at least equal or exceed city code requirements. In addition, code enforcement activities will have been used to remove substandard outbuildings in backyard areas and on corner lots. A number of these structures presently block the view of a number of the project's minor street intersections.
8. Final Project Configuration
The Configuration of the project as it will exist after completion of planned project activities and redevelopment is shown in the "Illustrative Site Plan," appendix J. The redeveloped areas are only approximations of the anticipated new construction, but they give a good idea of what the area will look like at some point in the future.
